verification.raw_trajectory_hash_recheck: Remote frozen driver hashes every training file before and after; raw trajectories are intentionally not copied into this laptop backup.

protocol: Five consecutive chronological saved-round updates36..40 from exact checkpoint35, one persistent GPU model/trainer/compiled graphs. Model/both Adam/PCG carry between updates; no resets, forced GC, clear_session or allocator flush between calls.
Same model, selective cuDNN, RL settings, batch512, both GPU cache payload caps8GiB, prepacking and canonical cache. No new games, source checkpoint writes or promoted weights.

Runtime/lifecycle diagnostic only: later saved behavior policies may differ from evolving diagnostic policy. Preserve guard decisions and full work counts; do not claim fresh on-policy learning strength or compare unequal-work speed.
Passive NVML/Linux sampling plus TensorFlow allocator current/peak and cache-lifetime observations. Distinguish allocator reserved high-water from live tensor bytes. No GPU trace.

All five complete finite with unchanged hashes/splits, uninterrupted optimizer/RNG states, bounded and released caches, no PPO worker/readers/cache-owned tensor references at boundaries. Last three post-update TF-current range<=256MiB; observed peak headroom>=2GiB is a separate operational gate, not a universal allocation guarantee.
No new game-generation workers: production worker coexistence and larger minibatches/rounds remain outside the test scope.
limitations: Saved rounds 37–40 were collected by historical policies that can differ from this uninterrupted diagnostic replay. This tests finite runtime lifecycle, shape variation and state continuity, not fresh on-policy learning or strength.
Five saved updates and these shapes establish finite runtime evidence only; they do not establish universal leak freedom, long-run stability or fresh on-policy learning strength.
No new game-generation workers run concurrently. Full production CPU-worker, producer and Windows-host memory coexistence remains unmeasured.
No baseline arm is included. Different guard proposal/accepted-step counts change work; observed update times are not a speedup estimate.
Logical input-cache payload caps exclude allocator bookkeeping, activations and workspaces. Physical NVML reservation may stay high after Python tensors and TF current allocations fall.
Tensor weakrefs observe Python cached Tensor wrappers, not every internal CUDA reference. TF current/peak and physical NVML provide complementary sampled evidence.

Cumulative raw physical GPU samples include between-update state evidence reads. Windows timestamps can step, so wall-clock alignment and curves are approximate; update durations are monotonic. Activity is not FLOPS/occupancy, reserved VRAM is not live tensor payload, and sampling may miss short peaks.

Linux PSI/swap/OOM counters are system-wide and may include unrelated work. Windows-host paging is not measured. RSS includes mapped pages and model/runtime memory; lifetime MaxRSS is not incremental cache memory.
At least2GiB sampled physical headroom is a separate operational criterion, not a guarantee against unsampled peaks or larger batches/rounds.
